{
  "method": "ensembles",
  "rationale": "Choose the first ranked feasible method, ensembles. The packet reports whole-workload concurrent throughput on one GPU with MPS, p=1 and k=bound=1.8112691325738948, capped by min(8, measured concurrency factor). This is a throughput bound, not a guaranteed speedup or an eightfold gain. Kernels account for 59.9042% of wall time and CUDA API host time for 39.6827%; H2D and D2H transfers total only 0.4130%. Concurrent independent seed replicas can exploit the measured concurrency benefit across the workload. GPU utilization is unavailable, so no utilization claim is inferred. Pipelining has only a 1.002069505516728 bound, and multi-GPU is infeasible with one GPU. Preserve the sealed ensemble method and scientific protocol.",
  "plan_steps": [
    "In a later implementation, wrap the existing simulation entry point with a bounded ensemble scheduler for the existing single input and exactly seeds 1000 through 1007. Run independent worker processes and isolated OpenMM contexts on the same GPU under MPS, with at most eight concurrent replicas and no changes to simulation physics or per-replica work.",
    "Preserve initial coordinates, velocity seed, Langevin seed, precision, integrator settings, step counts, sampling and reporting for each paired baseline and candidate replica. Keep each seed's outputs isolated, record completion and errors, and aggregate results in fixed seed order without mixing replica states or random streams.",
    "Account for process and context startup, MPS scheduling, CPU contention, GPU contention, synchronization, output I/O and final aggregation in the unchanged timing protocol. Compare completion throughput for the identical eight-replica workload on one GPU, using the existing sequential baseline and timing pairs; do not treat the bound as measured candidate performance.",
    "For each metric, form candidate-minus-sequential-baseline differences paired by input and seed. Retain all eight seed differences in each timing pair, then reduce repeated timing-pair differences to one median per seed before inference. Fixed-seed repetitions are not independent scientific samples.",
    "Apply the sealed paired-median confidence rule at joint 95% confidence across both metrics: the minimum and maximum of the eight per-seed differences must lie strictly inside the respective symmetric absolute margins, 38.64607384469149 kJ/mol for mean_potential_kj_mol and 103.46087706490006 kJ/mol for final_potential_kj_mol. Keep seeds, margins, sample sizes and protocol fixed; do not expand seeds or adapt tolerances after observing outputs. Accept only if sealed scientific and performance gates pass."
  ],
  "files_expected": [
    "Existing simulation entry point or ensemble orchestration file; exact path is not supplied in the packet.",
    "Existing benchmark and paired-equivalence evaluation files; exact paths are not supplied in the packet.",
    "Per-seed candidate result files and aggregate ensemble.json in the protocol's existing output layout; candidate paths are not supplied in the packet."
  ],
  "risks": [
    "Concurrent execution can alter floating-point ordering and stochastic trajectories despite identical paired seeds. Scientific equivalence concerns paired energy medians, not trajectory identity; independent contexts and correctly assigned random streams are essential.",
    "The absolute margins are baseline-only Monte Carlo standard errors derived from across-seed sample SD divided by sqrt(8), not published scientific tolerances or measured same-seed repeatability. Across-seed SD does not estimate paired-difference variance, so empirical power cannot be certified.",
